end.summary:
- Discussed neutralisation in antacids and stomach acid.
- Khushi explained that an acid and a mild base react to form salt and water, reducing burning.
- They distinguished neutralisation from evaporation and mentioned heat being released.
- Indicator colours and using an indicator to identify neutralisation versus dilution remained uncertain.
- Teach-back was not passed; the safety difference between antacids and mixing household cleaners was discussed but not fully resolved.
end.parentNote: Asha practised neutralisation through the antacid example and repeated the sequence: acid plus base forms salt and water, reducing the acid’s effect. Khushi also correctly distinguished evaporation from the heat released in a reaction. They mixed up indicator colours and could not yet use an indicator to tell neutralisation from dilution; this was not corrected by the end. At home, use turmeric or hibiscus water with safe, labelled household solutions only, and ask Khushi to record the colour change before and after adding each solution—never mix cleaning products.
